name: tabular_forecast_shuffled
title: The shuffled twin: the same hourly forecast split at random, scaled before the split and back-filled across the cut
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-tabular: the defective half of the time-series pair

expected.defect: the scaler is fitted on the whole matrix two lines before train_test_split
expected.why: the held-out hours contribute their own mean and variance to the standardisation the model trains on

expected.defect: a shuffled random split on an hourly series that lags.py parsed as dates and sorted by time
expected.why: each held-out hour keeps its two neighbouring hours in the training set, so the score measures interpolation between known points rather than forecasting

expected.defect: cross_val_score gets a bare HistGradientBoostingRegressor over `matrix`, which prepare() had already scaled outside any fold
expected.why: no fold refits the scaler, so every fold's training half carries statistics from its own validation half

unsupported.shape: a rolling window that includes the current row
unsupported.wouldBe: no catalogued rule; the target-in-feature family stops at MLV105, which is about the target column itself
unsupported.why: roll_mean_24 at time t contains the value at time t, so the model can read its own answer out of the feature

unsupported.shape: back-filling the warm-up rows a shift creates
unsupported.why: bfill copies later values backwards, which moves information across the cut in the opposite direction to the leak everyone looks for

unsupported.wouldBe: MLV106 covers train_test_split and random_split only; a shuffled KFold over the same rows is the same defect
unsupported.why: each fold trains on hours that come after the hours it is scored on

forbidden.why: nothing is fitted on test_x here: the one scaler is fitted on the full matrix before the split, which is MLV101's defect and not MLV102's
SEED is passed as random_state to the splitter, the folds and the regressor
both train_test_split and KFold pass random_state=SEED
the only metric is mean_absolute_error on a regression target
no ranking metric appears in this project
lags.py contains no split; the parse_dates and sort_values in it are the evidence for the finding in train.py, not defects of their own
